correctness.rationale: The antisymmetric marked state is an eigenvector with eigenvalue \(\Delta-2\); the symmetric marked state and uniform unmarked state form the stated two-dimensional block. Leakage vanishes exactly at \(t=2\pi k/\alpha\). At those times the phase condition reduces to \(e^{-i\pi k\beta}=(-1)^{k+1}\), which for reduced \(p/q\) is solvable exactly when \(p\) and \(q\) have opposite parity, with \(k=q(2s+1)\). The map \(\Delta\mapsto\beta\) is strictly increasing from \((-1,1)\), since its derivative has numerator \(8\Delta+16n>0\), and solving the resulting quadratic in \(\sqrt\Delta\) gives the displayed inverse formula. Fresh numerical substitution over several \(n,p,q\) ranges reproduced \(\beta=p/q\) and the phase identity; those finite checks support, but do not replace, the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact control question for a canonical spin network: it classifies every positive equal energy shift at fixed coupling, not merely one working shift, and gives all transfer times. The arithmetic parity law and dense spectrum distinguish it from a routine parameter substitution and provide a reusable boundary between exact transfer and failure.
residual_risks: The result concerns exact transfer under an idealized single-excitation XY model with equal marked shifts and fixed uniform couplings.

final_claim: For every \(n\ge4\), in the single-excitation complete-network Hamiltonian with every off-diagonal coupling equal to \(2\) and a common positive shift \(\Delta\) on two designated vertices, perfect state transfer between those vertices occurs exactly when \(\beta(\Delta)=(\Delta-2n)/\sqrt{(\Delta-2n)^2+16\Delta}=p/q\) in lowest terms with \(|p|<q\) and opposite parity. The positive transfer times are \(2\pi q(2s+1)/\alpha(\Delta)\), and inversion gives the stated dense countable family of shifts, including \(\Delta=2n\).
scientific_limitations: The classification is for equal positive shifts on exactly two designated vertices and uniform complete-network couplings.
No robustness statement for perturbed couplings or shifts is claimed.
